newsitem.title: USA: Public favors ABC in Food Lion case - poll.
newsitem.headline: Public favors ABC in Food Lion case - poll.

text.p: Most Americans sided with ABC News in its legal battle with Food Lion Inc., which won $5.5 million in punitive damages from the network last month over an undercover investigation of the supermarket chain, according to a poll released Wednesday

The survey conducted for the Media Studies Centre by the Roper Centre found that, of 1,001 Americans 18 and older polled nationwide, 514, or 51 percent, had heard of the court case, the Media Studies Centre said.

Of that group, 52 percent said they sided with ABC, part of Walt Disney Co. Twenty-one percent said they sided with Food Lion, a Salisbury, N.C.-based unit of Belgian retailer Ets Delhaize Freres et Cie "LE LION" SA.
The remaining 27 percent said they did not know whom they favoured.

Forty-nine percent of the entire survey group said they had not heard about the case, in which Food Lion accused the ABC News programme "PrimeTime Live" of using illegal methods to report a story about unsanitary food handling practices at a Food Lion supermarket.
The network is appealing the Jan. 22 decision by a federal jury in Greensboro, N.C.
Food Lion's lawsuit did not challenge the program's accuracy but focused instead on how ABC producers obtained jobs with the company and used concealed cameras while working for the supermarket.

Eighty percent of those who had heard of the case said they thought ABC was not doing anything out of the ordinary in employing the reporting techniques they used to get the Food Lion story, the Media Studies Centre said.
Fifty-nine percent thought the $5.5 million penalty was too severe, while 23 percent thought it was either about right and 7 percent felt it was not severe enough.
The random telephone survey had a margin of error of plus or minus 4.3 percentage points, meaning results could vary by that much either way.

The Media Studies Centre, based in New York, is part of The Freedom Forum, a foundation focusing on free press and free speech issues. The Roper Centre is a non-profit polling organisation based at the University of Connecticut in Storrs, Conn.
